title: Screening and Brief Intervention for Psychoactive Substance Use by Dentists in France
official: Assessment of and Training in Screening and Brief Intervention (SBI) for Psychoactive Substance Use by Dentists in France: a Mixed-Methods Study and Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: The use of psychoactive substances (tobacco, alcohol, cannabis) is widespread in France. Dentists, as primary care providers, are particularly well-positioned to implement screening and brief intervention (SBI). However, there are no data on their practices. This multicenter project (Brest, Tours) consists of two phases: 1) a mixed-methods assessment of screening and brief intervention practices among dentists in private practice in France (a qualitative study using semi-structured interviews, followed by a national online survey), 2) the development of a training program dedicated to screening and brief intervention through a Delphi consensus, a pilot feasibility study, and a randomized controlled trial comparing trained dentists with dentists practicing according to their usual practices. No patients are included. Only volunteer dentists participate in this project.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Volunteer dentists who have expressed non-opposition Qualified and currently practising

Exclusion Criteria:

Refusal to participate Non-qualified or retired dentists
